title: Nonlinear and Chaotic Dynamics of Two Dipolar-Coupled Anisotropic Spins under Periodic Excitation
abstract: We investigate the non-linear magnetization dynamics of two identical anisotropic macrospins coupled by dipolar interaction and subjected to periodic transverse excitation. The coupled Landau- Lifshitz-Gilbert equations are solved numerically using a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. By combining bifurcation diagrams, local-maxima analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and two-dimensional stability maps, we characterize how dipolar coupling, transverse driving amplitudes, and uniaxial anisotropy govern the long-time dynamics. The results reveal a non-monotonic reorganization of dynamical regimes, with alternating intervals of enhanced and suppressed instability. Analysis of symmetric and antisymmetric coordinates distinguishes the collective and relative spin responses, while Fourier spectra and three-dimensional trajectories provide complementary frequency-domain and geometrical characterizations. Simultaneous positivity of the two largest Lyapunov exponents identifies parameter regions consistent with hyperchaotic dynamics. Finally, analytical linearization and ferromagnetic-resonance calculations reveal the distinct coupling dependence of the collectivemode frequencies and clarify the limitations of the linearized description beyond the stability thresholds of the collinear reference state. These findings establish a unified framework for understanding the interplay of dipolar coupling, anisotropy, and periodic excitation in the non-linear dynamics of a minimal interacting-spin system.
summary: This paper analyzes the complex, non-linear dynamics of two interacting magnetic spins driven by an external oscillating field. By employing advanced chaos diagnostics, the authors map out parameter regimes exhibiting hyperchaotic behavior. The work establishes a unified understanding of how dipolar coupling and anisotropy jointly control the system's stability and response.
main_problem: The study investigates the non-linear and chaotic dynamics of two dipolar-coupled anisotropic spins subjected to periodic transverse excitation.
main_result: The dynamics exhibit a non-monotonic reorganization of dynamical regimes, with evidence of hyperchaotic dynamics in specific parameter regions.
method: The authors use numerical solutions of the coupled Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equations, supplemented by advanced diagnostics like Lyapunov exponents, bifurcation diagrams, and Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) calculations.
model_or_system: The model consists of two identical anisotropic macrospins coupled by a dipolar interaction and driven by a time-periodic transverse field. The dynamics are governed by the coupled Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equations.
key_observables: Lyapunov exponents, bifurcation diagrams, Fourier spectra, and the separation of dynamics into symmetric and antisymmetric collective coordinates.
important_parameters: Dipolar coupling strength, transverse driving amplitudes ($h_x, h_y$), and uniaxial anisotropy strength ($K$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on solving the LLG equation numerically and comparing results with analytical linearizations, noting limitations beyond the collinear reference state.
figures_summary: Figures summarize 2D maps of Lyapunov exponents across parameter planes (e.g., $D-h_x$), and show FMR responses and 3D magnetization trajectories for varying coupling strengths.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system's response by varying coupling strength and driving amplitudes, using multiple diagnostic tools (LEs, spectra, FMR) to characterize transitions between stable, quasi-periodic, and chaotic regimes.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed, quantitative framework for understanding how external driving and internal interactions (dipolar coupling) can induce complex, high-dimensional chaotic behavior in minimal magnetic systems, which has parallels in driven quantum oscillators.
